review: 1:4 לַחְמִי וּמֵימָי — John 6:35 (לֶחֶם הַחַיִּים) with John 4:14 (הַמַּיִם); the Arabic خُبْزِي وَالْمِيَاه and the order 'bread then water' are kept, because the stanza's argument is that He alone satisfies hunger.

2:3–2:4 אֵיךְ יִשַּׁח / סֹלֵחַ עָוֺן רַב — the Arabic كَيْفَ يَحْنُو / يَغْفِرُ الذَّنْبَ is 'how He bends low … forgiving'; שָׁחַח is the biblical verb for bowing (Ps 10:10), and the participle סֹלֵחַ keeps the continuous forgiving of Ps 103:3.
5:4 מִי כְדוֹדִי בָּאָדָם — Song 5:10 (דּוֹדִי … מְאֹד) turned into the Arabic's rhetorical أَيُّ شَخْصٍ كَحَبِيبِي; the Hebrew keeps the question form rather than an assertion.

3:3 וְזַעַף הַיָּם יִכְלָא — the Arabic وَجِمَاحَ الْبَحْرِ يَكْبَح is 'curbing the sea's surge'; כָּלָא ('restrain') is used of holding back waters in the biblical idiom, and זַעַף is the sea's raging (Jonah 1:15).
7:3 יִתְעַלֶּה וְיָרוּם — Isa 6:1 and 57:15 (רָם וְנִשָּׂא); the Arabic يَمْتَازُ وَيَعْلُو / شَامِخًا is that height, and the Hebrew keeps the doubled exaltation rather than one verb.
